stem: A hospital adds an electronic hand-hygiene monitoring system to its quality-improvement program. Which interpretation of the electronic data is most appropriate?

options.A: Use the system to broaden monitoring and identify adherence patterns, but interpret its data with knowledge of what behaviors the system can and cannot detect and validate findings with other methods when needed
options.B: Treat electronic compliance percentages as a perfect measure of every CDC hand-hygiene indication and of the quality of hand-cleaning technique
options.C: Stop all other auditing or feedback because electronic monitoring eliminates measurement limitations and observer bias completely
options.D: Assume a detected dispenser activation proves that hand hygiene occurred at every clinically indicated moment and was performed correctly

rationale: Electronic monitoring can expand the volume and continuity of adherence data and may reduce some limitations of episodic direct observation. However, monitoring systems differ in what they detect and may not capture every clinical indication, technique quality, or context. Infection-prevention programs should use standardized monitoring, understand method limitations, validate data, and provide feedback rather than treating any single metric as perfect ground truth.
educational_objective: Interpret electronic hand-hygiene monitoring as a quality-improvement tool with useful reach but important measurement limitations.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Infection Control Assessment and Response (ICAR) Tool; Isolation Precautions — Fundamental Elements
source_version_date: CDC web content current through 2024; accessed 2026

source_claim_supported: Electronic monitoring can support hand-hygiene quality improvement, but monitoring methods require validation and should not be treated as flawless measurement of all hand-hygiene behavior.

correction_summary: Removed the source's absolute claims of objective continuous superiority and elimination of Hawthorne-effect limitations. Rebuilt the item around appropriate interpretation, validation and complementary monitoring methods.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: CDC ICAR and infection-control technology guidance verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Electronic monitoring utility and method limitations are defensible; no unsupported perfect-objectivity claim remains.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; systems do not universally capture every indication/technique.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; a single method does not eliminate all measurement limitations.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; dispenser activation is not equivalent to every correctly performed indication.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A appropriately balances utility and limitations.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are interpretations of the monitoring data.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked direct-observation Hawthorne effect, sensor architectures, technique capture and quality-improvement use; no unresolved conflict.
